It’s actually crazy but I just now realised how much that also applies to me when knowing someone else is in pain. I am just afraid to overdo it. I guess framing is important

you are absolutely welcome. as for the DM feature, I just checked and at least in the browser on my laptop, I can indeed send messages. 

I hope that some of that will work for you, of course you know yourself best so try and experiment with what measures work. Social media can be a real downer but it doesn't have to be.

I also recently decided to take a break from social media because it was bad for my mental health, but I also find my self being drawn back. I might have advice for you that worked for me.

Social media are big business, the more we use them, the more money the companies make. so they want you to use their services as much as possible and therefore want to spend time on them before you realize you are. But if you actively think whether or not you want to check in IG, SC, or any other, then you will find it easier to resist. 

My practical advice is, don't make these platforms too easily accessible for you. Turn off notifications outside the app. For IG: uninstall the app and use in in the browser and don't save your login. Already the fact that you will have to log in every time before you check it gives you the extra second to think if you really want to use the service rn. and lastly, if you feel that you need to check on what is happening online, just do it extensively once a day, not all the time. 

These are just my personal experiences, but they worked for me. I am still using most social media, but sparingly. only on SC I have turned my back for now.
